Automations handle ongoing work, from daily briefings to release notes, without starting from scratch each time. Set the assignment once, choose a schedule or trigger, and let Computer pick up where it left off.

A scheduled task runs at a set time, like an industry digest every morning. A trigger-based automation starts when a condition is met in a supported app, like a new Gmail message or a Slack message in a selected channel. Each run uses the assignment and its history to build on prior work without repeating it.

Automations are designed for tasks that continue beyond a single prompt. Perplexity says users can schedule recurring work or trigger actions when events occur in connected apps. The system can use Memory, Skills and connectors, build on earlier runs, and pause for human review before consequential actions. Examples provided by the company include monitoring housing listings and price cuts, reacting to supplier-delay emails, and preparing follow-up work when a customer has not replied. # Perplexity Computer adds Automations for scheduled and event-driven work

Perplexity has expanded its Computer product with Automations, a feature for running recurring work on a schedule or responding to events in connected applications. The October 5 product update also adds inline interactive visualizations, access to GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 for eligible paid users, new video-generation options, and business Skills curated with American Express. The release is a broad product update rather than a single model launch, with Automations positioned as the main workflow change.

results.title: Perplexity Just Dropped Their Own OpenClaw And It Hits Hard
results.content:
Perplexity just released Perplexity Computer, a system built to push AI beyond search and into long-running autonomous work. Instead of answering prompts step by step, it executes full workflows end to end, handling research, planning, writing, coding, deployment, revisions, and ongoing management inside one coordinated environment. Models are treated as interchangeable tools, dynamically routed across reasoning, research, image, video, and fast-response tasks to keep work moving without constant supervision. With isolated compute environments, persistent memory, and real browser and filesystem access, Perplexity Computer is designed for projects that run for hours or days. This launch positions orchestration as the next competitive layer in AI and signals a shift toward AI operating as [...] [2:02] The coordination happens automatically in the background, so the work keeps moving forward while you step away instead of sitting there watching progress bars. One of the more important
[2:11] technical details is that Perplexity Computer is multimodel by design. As of launch, it can orchestrate work across
[2:18] 19 different AI models. There isn't one single model doing everything. Instead, different models are selected dynamically depending on the task.
[2:27] Reasoning tasks go to a reasoning focused [music] model. Research tasks go to a research optimized model. Image generation goes to an image model.
[2:35] [music] Video tasks go to a video model.
[2:37] Lightweight or fast operations can be routed to models optimized for speed. [...] 🚨 Why It Matters
This goes beyond automation. Perplexity Computer shows what happens when AI moves past chat and starts operating through real tools. By coordinating multiple models inside a managed environment, it removes friction that limited real-world use. With enterprise testing underway and Samsung integrating Perplexity into Galaxy devices, this points to AI shifting from an assistant into an operating layer that keeps work running in the background.
